title: The day's-cap guard (bin/paid-cost guard eval) still…
what: lib/relay_paidcap.py:179: MEDIUM: F2 the day's-cap guard (bin/paid-cost guard eval) still estimates the next batch as the largest stored one, so a grown suite passes the guard
why: Found 27 Oct by the review of wt/paid-estimate, outside that change: the paid-run estimate now adds new eval cases at the mean case cost (it estimates the 26 Oct run at $17.39 against an actual $17.43), but the day's-cap guard in lib/relay_paidcap.py still estimates a run from the largest stored batch, so it misses a suite that grew and can start a run that passes the $200 daily cap.
failing_case: The 26 Oct records before the $17.43 run: eval_estimate() returns $9.56 (largest full batch), while the suite had
grown from 15 to 27 cases. With $12 left in the day, the guard lets the run start; the --within-day ceiling then
stops it at about $12, part-way, instead of refusing it before it starts. The per-case estimate this change adds
($17.39 for that run) would have refused it.
pass_cases: 1. Records of 26 Oct before 01-47-23Z, suite of 27 cases, $12 left of the day's cap: guard eval exits 1 naming an
2. Same records, $30 left: guard eval exits 0.
3. No stored record: the estimate stays 0 and guard eval exits 0 (today's behaviour).
